runs.name: The Greenbrier Companies, Inc.; NYSE GBX, SEC CIK 0000923120, a freight railcar builder in North America, Europe and Brazil with wheel, parts and maintenance services and an owned lease fleet, in two segments, Manufacturing and Leasing & Fleet Management; Maintenance Services folded into Manufacturing from 2024-09-01; CEO retirement announced 2026-08-31, effective 2027-01-06; the 10-K names no rival, Trinity, FreightCar America and GATX read as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.entry: Price **$39.11** (quote of 2026-10-16 printed by `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged). Shares **30,939,686** at 2026-06-25 (cover of the 10-Q for the quarter to 2026-05-31, accession 0001193125-26-292719; one class; repurchased shares retired, no treasury stock; the 8-Ks of 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-22 change no count; the 2028 convertible notes, conversion about $55.10, not added); cap **$1,210.1M**. Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury daily par yield curve, 30-year, 2026-10-15). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (0001193125-25-253612), no FY2026 10-K on EDGAR at the fetch; 10-Q to 2026-05-31; DEF 14A filed 2025-11-17 (0001193125-25-284604); 10-Ks FY2024, FY2022, FY2021, FY2019 and FY2016; the 8-Ks of 2026-07-01, 2026-08-31 and 2026-09-22. Cross-check: FY2025 revenue $3,240.2M and operating cash $265.7M on the filed statements equal the tags, debt $1,750.9M equals the LongTermDebt tag. `tools/run.py`'s owner cash set aside: it does not add back the sale proceeds of lease-fleet railcars, so owner cash was recast by hand from twelve filed cash-flow statements. The brief departed in one stated place: the lines of evidence chosen by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7, stated under Step 0. **Q1 IN**: a cyclical freight-car builder in Mexico, the US, Europe and Brazil and a lessor of about 17,000 owned cars, the products the ones the FY2016 10-K names, deliveries over the cycle, margin per car, fleet utilization and capital put in readable from twelve years of filings. **Q2 OUT**: Manufacturing, 63% of FY2021 to FY2025 segment profit, decides, and it has commodity-type economics: a certified standard car sold to a few large buyers (two customers 26% of FY2025 revenue), price among the bases of competition, costs not all passed through, rivals that 'may sell products below cost' and new entrants named in Item 1A, FreightCar America moved to Mexico and profitable inside the span; segment margin 20.1% in FY2016, 3.9% in FY2021, 10.6% in FY2025; deliveries 20,300 in FY2016 and 20,400 in FY2025 while capital employed rose from $1,098M to $3,178M and after-tax earnings from operations fell from $306M to $270M; after-tax return on capital 9.9% mean FY2016 to FY2025, 7.9% without the FY2016 peak. GBX's manufacturing margin beat Trinity's rail products in seven of nine years from 2016 and FreightCar America's every year to 2023, credited but never showing in the returns; Trinity's rail products 0.4% to 9.6% of revenue 2018 to 2025, FreightCar America operating losses 2017 to 2022 and a $107.4M deficit at 2025-12-31, GATX 7.1% to 12.1% on equity 2018 to 2025. The 10-K names no rival; Trinity, FreightCar America and GATX chosen as a CONVENTION of the run. The 10-Q to 2026-05-31 shows third-quarter deliveries down 38.5%. Q3 to Q12 not reached. Facts after the stop: owner cash after all spending negative in seven of twelve years and in total; debt $304M to $1,751M against equity $874M to $1,532M, most of the rise non-recourse against a lease fleet grown from $306M to $1,329M; $373.8M convertible notes due April 2028; inventories faster than sales; Portland Harbor Superfund liability not estimable. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged** (DEF 14A): the CEO paid $7.71M for FY2025; 60% of performance shares vest on 'Company EBITDA' excluding the European closure costs; restructuring and exit charges recurring ($46.7M in FY2023, European plant closures in FY2025); the proxy asked to raise the 50M authorized shares; the segment basis recast three times in five years; the CEO's retirement announced 2026-08-31, effective 2027-01-06. Owner cash, all spending, FY2016 to FY2025: -$85.7M a year equity, -$55.2M all-equity; maintenance guess -$4.1M and +$26.4M. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: value **-$48.18 to -$33.79** a share (all-equity, cycle base; net debt $1,531.9M at 2026-05-31) against $39.11, no case earns the floor; a generous case beside (working capital and spending above depreciation ignored) $30.96, still below the price; fair **-$44.67 all-equity** (-$1.31 equity-only); not armed, the box being OUT at Q2. A CONVENTION of the run: a 25% tax shield on interest for the all-equity basis. Contamination declared by the analyst: one `Test Runs/` listing before the template copy showing the names of other 2026-10-16 runs (GATX, WAB, R, WLFC, AER), none opened, GATX used only from its own SEC filings; the opening commit subjects (WLFC); the memory index; none used. Commits 5542c4a8 (template), 711692db (Step 0, balance sheets, owner cash, Q1), c1194579 (Q2), 7955bb73 (close). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` 51 distinct ids, 20 quote-id pairs, PASS; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_check.py` 24 fragments, 21 matched, the 3 flagged being filing or proxy words ('in addition to patent protection', Trinity's 'primarily located in Mexico', the DEF 14A closure-cost list) quoted before an id that heads the next point, no slip, no missing id, no E-id. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) Q2 names no measure for the field's returns; (2) the low-cost exception and the ordinary-returns rule pull against each other when the better-margined builder still earns an ordinary return, read here as credited only where it shows in the returns; (3) specific (e) silent on a lessor's recurring fleet sales and fleet capex in the maintenance case; (4) specific (b)'s halves rate on a series that changes sign within each half. Could not get: a FY2026 10-K; Trinity's 2017 and 2018 figures; the press release of the 2026-08-31 8-K; the Forms 144 and 4.
runs.narr: OUT at Q2 after Q1 IN (a cyclical freight-car builder and lessor of about 17,000 owned cars). Manufacturing decides and has commodity-type economics: a certified standard car sold to a few large buyers, two customers 26% of FY2025 revenue, rivals that may sell below cost and an entrant that crossed the barrier inside the span; deliveries 20,300 in FY2016 and 20,400 in FY2025 while capital employed tripled to $3,178M and after-tax earnings from operations fell from $306M to $270M; after-tax return on capital 9.9% mean, 7.9% without the FY2016 peak; better margins than Trinity in seven of nine years, credited, never shown in the returns; the field ordinary (Trinity rail products 0.4% to 9.6%, FreightCar America losses 2017 to 2022, GATX 7.1% to 12.1% on equity). Facts after the stop: owner cash after all spending negative in total over twelve years, debt $304M to $1,751M mostly non-recourse against the lease fleet; integrity facts recorded, not judged: pay on 'Company EBITDA' excluding closure costs, recurring exit charges, the CEO retiring 2027-01-06. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value -$48.18 to -$33.79 all-equity against $39.11, no case earning the floor; fair -$44.67 all-equity, -$1.31 equity-only, not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: no measure for the field's returns; the low-cost exception against the ordinary-returns rule; a lessor's fleet sales in the maintenance case; the halves rate on a series changing sign.
